title: Congruence

findings.finding: Extend the congruence result to show that the midpoint cut is perpendicular to the base.
findings.breakdown: The follow-up connects equal corresponding angles in the congruent triangles with adjacent angles on a straight line.
findings.checked: SSS gives triangle ACM congruent to triangle BCM, with M corresponding to M. Thus angles AMC and BMC are equal. Since A, M and B are collinear, these angles sum to 180°, so each is 90°. With AB = 10 cm, AM = 5 cm. Omit the proposed CM calculation: it requires Pythagoras, whose availability is not established by the supplied teaching.
findings.assumptions: Midpoint and angles on a straight line are prior knowledge. No calculator is needed.

repair.proposal: Append optional parts to p15-q13: (c) Now let AC = BC = 13 cm and AB = 10 cm. Find AM. Answer: 5 cm. (d) Explain why angle AMC is 90°. Answer: corresponding angles AMC and BMC are equal because the triangles are congruent; they sum to 180° because A, M and B lie on a straight line, so each is 90°.

findings.doneWhen: The optional follow-up uses the established congruence to justify perpendicularity, with the unsupported Pythagoras calculation omitted.
